The lists sort, filter and search from their own headings, and History's columns move and widen. Closed findings move into History, Trash and Conflicts count what they hold in tiles, and every button takes the accent under the pointer. A mirror to Windows replaces read-only files again, the kind Git leaves in every working copy.

## 🎨 Design

- **The lists in History, Trash, Conflicts and Anomalies sort, filter and search from their own headings.** A click on a heading sorts, the ▾ beside it filters, and typing in the list, or Ctrl+F, opens a search that floats over the list until Escape closes it; on a touch screen a magnifier at the end of the headings opens it. A filter or a search that narrows a list says so above it, with Show everything to undo it. A line under the headings explains all this on hover, and once by itself on the first visit. The Filter and Search buttons over History are gone.
- **A job's Files touched filters and searches from the head of its list too.**
- **Closed findings live in History,** as a third view beside Runs and Files with the findings closed in the last thirty days, filtered by severity and job from the headings. Anomalies shows only what is open, without the Open or closed selector, and leads to History when something was closed. The phone app does the same.
- **The columns in History and a job's Files touched can be moved and widened,** as in KnightLoader: drag a heading and the columns make room while you drag, drag the line at any column's edge to change its width, and double-click the line for the original width. Every line keeps to its column on one line, cut at the end. Each list keeps its arrangement in the browser.
- **A heading's filter opens under its ▾ over the dimmed and blurred page,** like every other window, and never over the sidebar or below the page; a long list of choices scrolls inside it and stands lower. Its choices stand side by side where they fit and under each other where not.
- **Trash and Conflicts count what they hold in tiles,** like Anomalies: the trash in three for all of it and each side, the conflicts in four for all of them and each kind. A tile shows its part alone, and the ▾ at the Job heading narrows the list to one job, however many jobs there are. The phone app has the same chips and the job filter in the list's head.
- **The three answers to a conflict stand in the order of the sides:** keep the left version, keep both, keep the right version, on the web and on the phone, and the answers for all of them under More follow the same order.
- **The phone app's History sorts and filters from the headings of its list.** A tap on a heading sorts, its ▾ opens the filter, and the magnifier at the end of the row opens the search. The Filter, Sort and Search buttons above it are gone.
- **Every button takes the accent when the pointer or the keyboard reaches it.** A grey button mixes a little of the accent into its ground and turns its symbol to the accent, while its words keep their colour. A button that is a symbol alone turns the symbol. On the phone a grey button does the same while your finger is on it.
- **Advanced in a job's settings is a button with a ground of its own,** like every other button with words, so it no longer reads as a heading.
- **The F-Droid button in Settings › Apps wears F-Droid's logo as GlimStone carries it,** flat in its own greens and blue, with the eyes still cut out.
- **Check for updates in Settings › Info wears the sync symbol,** as in KnightLoader; the cloud stays with fetching an update.
- **A finding on the Anomalies page has no coloured edge any more,** on the web and on the phone. Its badge says how bad it is.
- **Sizes stand at the start of their column,** with their heading, in History, a job's Files touched and the trash.
- **The duplicate search's buttons say what they do:** Find duplicates on the left side and Find duplicates on the right side.
- **ArrowLoop follows GlimStone 3.8.3.**

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A mirror to a Windows folder replaces read-only files again.** Git writes its objects and commit graphs read-only, and a job that carries file attributes copies that along. The next change to such a file failed on every run with access denied, because Windows refuses to rename a new copy over a read-only file, so a backup of a Git working copy ended every run with a warning.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Every new text is in all 42 languages.**
